gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room for another desk in here.
A large ___ of students have applied this year.
gaps.explanation: 'A large number of students' is used with countable plurals; 'amount' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: ___ the rooms in the hotel have a sea view; the rest face the car park.
gaps.explanation: Before 'the rooms' a partitive is needed: Some of; 'all/none' contradict the context.

gaps.sentence: ___ words, the plan is too expensive.
gaps.explanation: 'In other words' is the fixed phrase for rephrasing; 'another' cannot modify the plural 'words'.

gaps.sentence: There are trees on ___ side of the road.
gaps.hint: singular noun: each of the two sides
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means each of the two sides; 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.

gaps.sentence: Very ___ applicants had the required experience.
gaps.hint: 'very' + negative quantifier with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Very few' means almost none and is used with countables; 'very a few' is impossible.
